rationale: In the initial cohort defining KLHL20 neurodevelopmental disorder (Sleyp et al., 2022), 11 of 14 patients harbored the recurrent de novo missense variant p.Gly357Arg. Across the cohort, core presentation is characterized by intellectual disability, autism spectrum disorder, and hyperactivity, whereas seizures occurred in a subset (reported in 9 of the individuals assessed across the expanded/associated presentations) and were predominantly variable (febrile seizures or responsive epilepsy rather than uniform refractory afebrile epileptic encephalopathy; severe West syndrome was noted in a patient with a novel variant rather than the recurrent p.Gly357Arg variant).

evidence.text: Sleyp et al. delineated a genetic syndrome in 14 patients with de novo missense variants in KLHL20, finding 11 patients with the recurrent variant c.1069G>A p.(Gly357Arg). Patients presented consistently with intellectual disability, autism spectrum disorder, and hyperactivity, with febrile seizures or epilepsy reported as variable features.

source.title: De novo missense variants in the E3 ubiquitin ligase adaptor KLHL20 cause a developmental disorder with intellectual disability, epilepsy, and autism spectrum disorder
source.quote: We studied 14 patients with de novo missense variants in KLHL20, delineating a genetic syndrome with patients having mild to severe intellectual disability, febrile seizures or epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder, hyperactivity, and subtle dysmorphic facial features. We observed a recurrent de novo missense variant in 11 patients (NM_014458.4:c.1069G>A p.[Gly357Arg]).

evidence.text: At the 55th ESHG conference presentation, seizure manifestations were noted in 9 individuals among the cohort, and ClinGen curation documents an individual presenting with severe epileptic encephalopathy (West syndrome) as carrying a novel variant rather than the recurrent p.Gly357Arg.
